standard_prerequisites.use: The closed-immersion characterization lemma of the same chapter (collected as L16040), the open-locus result for unramified universally injective maps (lemma-where-unramified-universally-injective), and permanence of universal closedness (Morphisms of Spaces).

core_obligations: Establish universal closedness of f and all its base changes.
Verify the hypotheses of the unramified/injective open-locus lemma via the fibre product square.
Intersect the resulting open loci to isolate the closed-immersion functor.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce closed immersion to the three-factor characterization.
Universally closed permanence checks the hypothesis of the locus lemma.

difficulty_reason: Given a commutative diagram of algebraic spaces X -> Y -> Z with X -> Z locally of finite type and universally closed and Y -> Z separated, the lemma produces an open subspace W of Z such that a map Z' -> Z factors through W exactly when the base-changed map X_{Z'} -> Y_{Z'} is a closed immersion. The retained proof is written: use the chapter's characterization of closed immersions as universally closed, unramified and universally injective maps (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion, collected earlier as L16040); the map f is universally closed by permanence (Morphisms of Spaces, lemma-universally-closed-permanence) and stable under base change; it remains to feed the unramified-and-injective locus lemma (lemma-where-unramified-universally-injective) whose hypotheses are verified by showing X x_Y X -> Z is universally closed via base change and composition of universally closed maps. Retained author proof at lines 11661-11684.

dedup.scope: Openness of the closed-immersion locus for universally closed finitely type sources over separated targets.
